speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms: do you experience true spinning vertigo, or just a sense of unsteadiness? Also, have you noticed any recent hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) or vestibular migraine; however, given the constant nature and garlic intake, I must rule out Meniere's disease or viral labyrinthitis. REQUEST TEST: Audiometry. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Internal Auditory Canals.
